assessment: This study addresses both commonly accepted and alternative hypotheses for the mechanism by which an intercrop supports pest control in push–pull agriculture, a promising and broadly recognized approach for sustainable intensification. The findings address a widely recognized gap in data on the mechanism underlying push–pull systems and thus can be important for work on pest control in agroecology as well as plant–herbivore interactions more generally. The support of claims is solid, combining observations of several different mechanistic aspects in an uncommonly broad range of relevant environments with clear reasoning regarding experimental design.
